newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan retail petrol price steady at 105 yen/litre.
newsitem.headline: Japan retail petrol price steady at 105 yen/litre.

text.p: The average retail price of gasoline at petrol stations in Japan as of November 10 was 105 yen per litre, the fourth consecutive month the price has remained the same, a survey released on Monday showed.
The survey, conducted regularly by the Oil Information Service Centre, showed that the highest price was 116 yen and the lowest was 99 yen, a gap of 17 yen.
Refiners have raised oil product wholesale prices recently to take into account both climbing global crude oil prices and the yen's weakness against the dollar.
However, retail prices have not followed suit because of competition among gasoline stations and opposition from consumers.
The national average retail price of gas oil, mainly used by trucks and buses for fuel, was 82 yen per litre, up one yen from a month earlier. It was the first month-on-month rise since April.
